lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: Quiet turns can be revealing, and this one tells you the Maple Leafs are trying to build chemistry before the season even starts. The headliner is the Arizona getaway - a deliberate break from the old routine, with John Chayka calling it a fresh start and Auston Matthews hosting the club at home before a workout at Mullett Arena. Toronto's offseason ledger is clean, the record reset to 0-0, and that's the point: the club is trying to turn a long summer into a sharper fall. Gavin McKenna is the other live wire. The No. 1 pick has already flashed in preseason, looked comfortable, and now gets his first regular-season test next Tuesday against Montreal. What matters next is how quickly this new core hardens into a lineup, and whether McKenna forces the issue immediately.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The winter starts with a star talking like a man who knows the bill comes due. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. stood by his contract comments and, in the process, gave the Blue Jays' offseason its first sharp edge - a reminder that a 14-year, $500 million deal is never just a celebration, it is a daily examination. That is the story now, not the finished season; Toronto's year is over, and the work shifts to repair, not rescue. Guerrero's own words were plain: he feels the weight of every missed swing, every at-bat that does not match the price tag. That is where the franchise lives today, with its centerpiece under a bright, unforgiving light. Watch the club's next move around Guerrero - because his tone, and Toronto's response to it, will shape the entire offseason.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The offseason has one clear center of gravity now - Kawhi Leonard's arrival and commitment, not as rumor but as reality. The Raptors confirmed Leonard's multi-year extension on Wednesday, and that changes the temperature in the building even if the city is still waiting for camp and the first real look at the new order. Toronto finished 46-36 last season, a respectable base, but the real story is what comes next: whether RJ Barrett becomes a pillar or a pressure point, and whether Collin Murray-Boyles can grow into the long-term center question that has shadowed this roster for years. Leonard's deal says the front office believes the window is open. Training camp will tell whether this is a contender's blueprint or just a prettier paper stack.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: Sam Cosmi's absence has turned a routine September week into a gut-check on the right side of the line - and that's before Jayden Daniels' elbow and Nick Cross' illness widen the headache. Washington is 0-2, but the record matters less than the wreckage: the quarterback is out, the interior protection is wobbling, and the latest injury report left 14 players limited or not practicing. That is not a camp nuisance. That is a roster under stress. If Cosmi can't go, the Commanders will be patching the right guard spot with duct tape and nerve. Dan Quinn has no luxury here; he needs Marcus Mariota to steady the offense while the staff sorts through a line that can't keep taking body blows. Watch the injury report and the right-guard fix - those two answers will tell you whether Washington can even get through the next week intact.

article.title: Thursday's Skate
paragraphs: The Maple Leafs are flying to Arizona after Thursday's skate, with an open practice set for Saturday at ASU's Mullett Arena as part of a team-bonding trip before Opening Night. For the Blue Jays, Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is back in the spotlight after standing by his comments about his contract and saying, simply, that "what I said is the way I feel."

The Raptors remain in deep offseason mode, with fresh optimism built around RJ Barrett and a closer look at how he fits into 2026-27. In Washington, the Commanders are dealing with an injury cloud at right guard Sam Cosmi ahead of Seattle, and the conversation has already turned to who would step in if he cannot go.
